title: The Fruit Of Tariffs Is Fraud
gist: Gavekal Dragonomics argues reported US imports from China (US$276bn) hide a true flow likely above US$600bn because of fraud and re-routing, so eight years of tariffs have produced statistical rather than real decoupling.

themes.theme: Tariff evasion and the data illusion

insights.claim: US Customs data shows imports from China and Hong Kong at US$276bn over the past 12 months versus US$550bn in late 2018, which would put China below Canada, Mexico, Asean and the EU as import sources.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Headline decoupling data may overstate the shift away from China; treat official import shares with caution.

insights.claim: Gavekal estimates the true value of Chinese-made goods entering the US is likely above US$600bn annually, more than twice reported, because exporters and importers minimise tariffs through fraud and re-routing.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tariff effectiveness is lower than assumed, raising odds of further enforcement or new tariffs such as the Section 301 probe.
insights.quote: The true value of Chinese-made goods flowing into the US is likely in excess of US$600bn annually

insights.claim: US-China tensions have eased somewhat, with a mutual tariff reduction on some goods after the presidential summit, yet a new Section 301 investigation on 'structural excess capacity' remains underway.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Truce is partial; trade-policy risk persists.

insights.claim: The author calls the appearance of material decoupling a fiction, arguing the US continues to import huge quantities of Chinese goods obscured by fraud and re-routing.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Third-country transshipment hubs (e.g. Asean, Mexico) may carry inflated trade growth.
